subject: Safeguard exception: lockstep on A/B plan + acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Sam Collins <sam.collins@brightedge.co>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kathy Nguyen <kathy@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning on A/B plan + acceptance criteria for promptset evaluation

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a tight timeline to validate the new promptset across our support ticket summarization flow and want to lock down the A/B plan + acceptance criteria so procurement and my PM can sign off. High level asks:

- Confirm sample size and traffic split for a 2-week canary.
- Define the acceptance criteria that would fail the rollout (precision/recall delta, latency, and hallucination thresholds).
- Any infra / batching constraints on Redwood's side we should account for during the canary.

Can we get a short mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday? I've attached our internal product checklist (AB_plan_v1.xlsx) that shows our preferred cadence.

Best,
Sam
Sam Collins
Product Lead, BrightEdge
attachments: AB_plan_v1.xlsx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Collins <sam.collins@brightedge.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on A/B plan + acceptance criteria for promptset evaluation

Thanks Sam — looping in Karthik and Dev for infra and evaluation constraints. Quick answers up front:

- Suggested split: 10% treatment / 90% control for first 3 days (smoke), then 25/75 for the remainder if no signal breaches.
- Minimum sample: 10k impressions per arm to hit our pre-specified eval power for the metrics you care about.
- Immediate kill criteria (examples we propose):
  * >= 4% absolute increase in hallucination rate (on the promptset gold) over control across two consecutive days.
  * >= 25% relative increase in 95th percentile latency per request sustained for 6 hours.
  * Any PII leakage instance verified by manual triage.

Karthik / Dev — can you confirm the feasibility of 10k impressions per arm with continuous batching enabled and whether we should advise them about tokenization changes? Also, please note the AB_plan_v1.xlsx that Sam sent — we attached a lightweight acceptance_checklist.md with the items we usually require.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | grace.oconnor@redwood.com
attachments: acceptance_checklist.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 14:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on A/B plan + acceptance criteria for promptset evaluation

Grace / Sam — quick technical check from infra/eval side.

- Feasibility: 10k impressions per arm over 2 weeks is fine from a serving perspective; continuous batching + prefix caching will keep cost low. If brightedge has long conversations (median > 1k tokens) we should account for additional latency.
- Tokenization: If the new promptset includes different special tokens, we need to pin the tokenizer across both arms — otherwise metric drift will be confounded. Recommend they lock tokenizer v2.
- Measurement: we will run an automated hallucination classifier + manual adjudication sample. For the kill rule on hallucinations, propose this exact wording be added to the checklist: "hallucination failure = validated hallucination rate in treatment > control by >= 4% absolute on the blinded adjudication set (p < 0.05) across a 48-hour window."

Open questions for product:
- Who signs final pass/fail? Product (Marissa) or the customer?
- Do we need a temporary SLA exception for the 95th pctl latency bump during the canary? That affects routing/fallback policy.

Related: filed SUP-987 to track the experiment and linked the plan: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB_ExampleDoc

Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE (Inference) | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning on A/B plan + acceptance criteria for promptset evaluation

Thanks everyone — signed off on the mutual action plan with two clarifications:

1) Product will be final arbiter for pass/fail, but we will include a 24-hour pause window to allow manual adjudication before a full rollback. Customer can request expedited manual review but must provide evidence samples.
2) We will grant a temporary SLA exception for a 95th pctl latency increase up to 30% for up to 12 hours during the canary; any sustained degradation beyond that triggers automatic fallback to control.

Grace — can you and Karthik update acceptance_checklist.md with the exact kill-rule language he suggested and add the tokenizer pin note? Once that's updated I'll route to legal/procurement for the procurement checklist and signature.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
